thread:
maria (docs): hey team - quick sync. i opened a docs PR for SOC2 language around audit log archival and restore. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/512
samir (legal): saw it, thanks. quick note: legal prefers we separate 'retention' from 'archival restore timelines' in wording. keep it concrete but not a promise of uptime for archived retrieval.
elaine (product): can you paste the proposed snippet here? i'll check product alignment for retention tiers.
ryan (eng): fwiw, runtime behavior: hot logs (indexed) are available for immediate query for 30 days, cold archives moved to blob storage and searchable after a restore job (expected restore time SLA: 48-72 hrs).
samir (legal): this is good. our recommended doc phrasing: `We retain audit logs in a high-availability indexed store for 30 days. Older logs are moved to encrypted archival storage where they are retained for up to 12 months. Restores from archival storage are supported; typical restoration completes within 48–72 hours. For regulated customers requiring longer retention, contact support for a Dedicated or Private solution.`
maria (docs): thanks. can we make a short FAQ entry that avoids absolutes like "guaranteed"? also need a short code/config snippet example for the retention table.
elaine (product): yes: small FAQ Q/A + a short table mapping tier -> default retention -> restore time estimate.
ryan (eng): sample config snippet for the platform team (internal example):

```
{
  "audit_retention": [
    {"tier": "hot", "duration_days": 30, "searchable": true},
    {"tier": "archive", "duration_days": 365, "searchable": false, "restore_window_hours": 72}
  ]
}
```

maria (docs): perfect. i'll add that. samir, can you confirm the wording below for the public docs? i want to keep it short and compliance-friendly.

Proposed public paragraph:
"We store audit logs in a high-availability store for 30 days to enable immediate querying and incident investigation. After 30 days, logs transition to encrypted archival storage and are retained for up to 12 months. Customers may request archival restores; typical restores complete within 48–72 hours. For bespoke retention needs beyond 12 months or for the data residency requirements, please contact support or consider Redwood Dedicated/Private deployments."

samir (legal): LGTM with one tweak: replace "may request" with "can request" and remove "typical" before restore time to avoid hedging. suggest: `Customers can request archival restores; restores generally complete within 48–72 hours.`
maria (docs): updated in PR. also adding an FAQ entry: "How long are audit logs retained and how quickly can archived logs be restored?" with the paragraph + config example + link to enterprise options.
elaine (product): add a short note about exportability: "Customers can export audit logs at any time during hot retention. Exports from archived logs are subject to the same restore process."
ryan (eng): ops-bot will append the archival retention SLA metadata to the customer tenant UI once PR merges; will require a small backend flag. tagging @ops-bot to confirm.
ops-bot: automated check: docs PR 512 - build passed, link checks ok. reminder: add internal note referencing ticket INF-2043 for backend flag.
maria (docs): thanks all — i'll push the change, merge when CI green. leaving the PR open for any last wording tweaks. :thumbsup:
